usage: Used for playing a musical instrument (suonare il pianoforte, la chitarra) and for bells, phones and alarms ringing (il telefono suona). Do not confuse with 'giocare', which is for games and sports. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Mia sorella suona il pianoforte da cinque anni.
examples.en: My sister has been playing the piano for five years.

examples.it: Ieri sera abbiamo suonato fino a mezzanotte.
examples.en: Last night we played until midnight.

examples.it: Quando suonerà la campanella, potrete uscire.
examples.en: When the bell rings, you can go out.

usage: Synonym of 'chiedere' for asking questions or asking about someone; for requesting objects or favours 'chiedere' is more common. Note the indirect object: 'domandare a qualcuno'. The reflexive 'domandarsi' means to wonder. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Ti domando solo una cosa: sei felice?
examples.en: I ask you only one thing: are you happy?

examples.it: Il professore mi ha domandato dove abito.
examples.en: The teacher asked me where I live.

examples.it: Domanderò a Luca se viene con noi.
examples.en: I will ask Luca if he is coming with us.

usage: The verb for introducing people to each other ('Ti presento Marco') and for presenting a project, a programme or a document. Regular -are verb; the reflexive 'presentarsi' means to introduce oneself or to show up.

examples.en: Let me introduce you to my sister Anna.

examples.it: Ieri Marco mi ha presentato i suoi genitori.
examples.en: Yesterday Marco introduced me to his parents.

examples.it: Domani presenterò il mio progetto alla classe.
examples.en: Tomorrow I will present my project to the class.

usage: Learned first through its imperatives: 'Scusa' (informal), 'Scusi' (formal) and 'Scusate' (plural), used both to apologise and to get someone's attention. 'Scusa se...' introduces an apology. Regular -are verb; the reflexive 'scusarsi' means to apologise.

examples.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

examples.it: Scusa se non ti ho chiamato ieri.
examples.en: Sorry I didn't call you yesterday.

examples.it: Spero che il professore mi scusi per il ritardo.
examples.en: I hope the teacher will excuse me for being late.

usage: The verb for the midday meal; 'pranzare da qualcuno' means having lunch at someone's place. Italians typically pranzano between 12:30 and 2 pm. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Di solito pranzo a mezzogiorno e mezzo.
examples.en: I usually have lunch at half past twelve.
On Sunday we had lunch at our grandparents'.
Tomorrow we will have lunch in the canteen.

usage: The verb for the evening meal; 'cenare fuori' means eating out. In Italy people cenano rather late, around 8 pm. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Tonight we are having dinner at eight.

examples.it: Ieri sera ho cenato con i colleghi.
examples.en: Last night I had dinner with my colleagues.
Would you have dinner with me on Saturday?

usage: To draw with a pencil or pen, and also to design objects, clothes or buildings. Regular -are verb; the noun 'disegno' means both drawing and design.

examples.en: My son always draws animals.

examples.it: Ho disegnato una mappa per te.
examples.en: I drew a map for you.

examples.it: Se disegnassi meglio, farei il fumettista.
examples.en: If I drew better, I would be a comic artist.

usage: To add colour to a drawing or an object; the colour is introduced by 'di' (colorare il cielo di blu). Regular -are verb; common with children (album da colorare).

examples.it: I bambini colorano il disegno con i pastelli.
examples.en: The children colour in the drawing with crayons.

examples.it: Ho colorato il cielo di blu.
examples.en: I coloured the sky blue.

examples.it: Colora le pareti di giallo, così la stanza sarà più luminosa.
examples.en: Colour the walls yellow, so the room will be brighter.

usage: Used with or without an object (fumare una sigaretta / non fumo). You will see it on signs: 'Vietato fumare'. 'Smettere di fumare' means to quit smoking. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I don't smoke, thanks.

examples.it: Ha fumato per vent'anni, poi ha smesso.
examples.en: He smoked for twenty years, then he quit.
If you smoked less, you would breathe better.

usage: Regular -are verb, but note the spelling of the 'tu' form 'scii' with two i's (scio, scii, scia, sciamo, sciate, sciano). 'Andare a sciare' is the usual way to say 'to go skiing'.

examples.en: Can you ski?

examples.it: L'inverno scorso abbiamo sciato sulle Dolomiti.
examples.en: Last winter we skied in the Dolomites.
At Christmas we will ski in Cortina.

usage: Used to say how long something lasts: 'Quanto dura il film?'. Takes essere in compound tenses (è durato). Regular -are verb; the related noun is 'la durata'.

examples.en: The film lasts two hours.

examples.it: La lezione è durata più del previsto.
examples.en: The lesson lasted longer than expected.
How long will the journey take?

usage: The opposite of 'amare'; followed directly by a noun or an infinitive (odio alzarmi presto). Regular -are verb: odio, odi, odia. Often used informally for strong dislikes, not only real hatred.

examples.en: I hate getting up early.
As a child I hated vegetables.

examples.it: Non credo che mi odi davvero.
examples.en: I don't think he really hates me.

en: to stroll; to go for a walk
usage: Walking for pleasure, as opposed to 'camminare' (walking in general). 'Fare una passeggiata' is an equally common alternative. Regular -are verb; the i is dropped before e/i (passeggi, passeggerò).

examples.en: On Sundays we stroll around the centre.

examples.it: Ieri ho passeggiato lungo il fiume.
examples.en: Yesterday I walked along the river.
We will take a little walk after dinner.

usage: Regular -are verb; the i is dropped before e/i (abbracci, abbraccerò). The reciprocal 'abbracciarsi' means to hug each other. Letters and messages often end with 'un abbraccio'.

examples.it: Abbraccio forte i miei figli ogni sera.
examples.en: I hug my children tight every evening.
We hugged each other at the station.
When you arrive, I will hug you tight.

usage: Regular -are verb; the i is dropped before e/i (baci, bacerò). The reciprocal 'baciarsi' means to kiss each other. In Italy friends greet each other with two kisses on the cheeks.

examples.it: In Italia si bacia due volte sulle guance.
examples.en: In Italy people kiss twice on the cheeks.
He kissed her in front of everyone.

examples.it: Bacerò i bambini prima di partire.
examples.en: I will kiss the children before leaving.

en: to photograph; to take a picture of
usage: Takes a direct object (fotografare il mare). In everyday speech 'fare una foto a qualcuno' is at least as common. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I like photographing sunsets.
I photographed the whole city.

examples.it: Fotograferemo la torta prima di tagliarla.
examples.en: We will take a picture of the cake before cutting it.

usage: Everyday verb for throwing, especially throwing things away ('buttare via', 'buttare la spazzatura'). Colloquial expression: 'buttare un occhio' (to have a quick look). Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I take out the rubbish every evening.

examples.it: Hai buttato via il giornale di ieri?
examples.en: Did you throw away yesterday's newspaper?

examples.it: Butterei tutto, ma mia madre vuole tenere ogni cosa.
examples.en: I would throw everything away, but my mother wants to keep everything.

usage: Always with the preposition 'a': 'bussare alla porta', 'bussare alla finestra'. Regular -are verb, takes avere.

examples.en: Someone is knocking at the door.

examples.it: Ho bussato tre volte, ma nessuno ha aperto.
examples.en: I knocked three times, but nobody opened.

examples.it: Bussa prima di entrare, per favore.
examples.en: Knock before coming in, please.

usage: Reflexive verb describing the moment of falling asleep, as opposed to 'dormire' (to sleep). Takes essere; the participle agrees with the subject. Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Mi addormento sempre davanti alla TV.
examples.en: I always fall asleep in front of the TV.

examples.it: Ieri sera i bambini si sono addormentati subito.
examples.en: Last night the children fell asleep right away.

examples.it: Se bevi il caffè adesso, non ti addormenterai.
examples.en: If you drink coffee now, you won't fall asleep.

usage: Part of the morning-routine reflexives (lavarsi, vestirsi, pettinarsi). With a body part the article is used, not the possessive: 'mi pettino i capelli'. Regular -are verb; the non-reflexive 'pettinare' means to comb someone else's hair.

examples.en: I comb my hair in front of the mirror.

examples.it: Ti sei pettinata? Hai i capelli in disordine.
examples.en: Did you comb your hair? It's messy.
Comb your hair before going out!

usage: Reflexive verb of the daily routine; the non-reflexive 'truccare' means to make someone else up. Spelling change: an h is added before e/i (ti trucchi, mi truccherò). Takes essere.

examples.it: Non mi trucco mai per andare al lavoro.
examples.en: I never put on make-up to go to work.

examples.it: Si è truccata per la festa.
examples.en: She put on make-up for the party.

examples.it: Se ti trucchi troppo, sembri più vecchia.
examples.en: If you wear too much make-up, you look older.

en: to come back; to get home
usage: Very common for coming back home or back to work after being out or away: 'rientrare a casa', 'rientrare dalle vacanze'. Takes essere. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I always get home at seven.
They came back from holiday yesterday.
What time will you be back tonight?

usage: To lend something to someone; the borrower is introduced by 'a'. Do not confuse with 'prendere in prestito' (to borrow). Fixed phrase: 'prestare attenzione' (to pay attention). Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Will you lend me your pen?

examples.it: Ho prestato dieci euro a Luca.
examples.en: I lent Luca ten euros.

examples.it: Ti presterei il libro, ma l'ho già promesso a Sara.
examples.en: I would lend you the book, but I have already promised it to Sara.

usage: The verb for giving back something borrowed or bought; the person is introduced by 'a'. Takes -isc- in the present (restituisco, restituisci). Regular -ire verb.

examples.en: I'll give you the book back tomorrow.
They gave the money back right away.
I will return everything by Friday.

usage: To pour a liquid (versare il vino nel bicchiere) and, in banking, to pay money into an account. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Pour the water into the glass.

examples.it: Ho versato il latte nella tazza.
examples.en: I poured the milk into the cup.
I will pay my salary into the account.

en: to erase; to delete; to cancel
usage: Covers erasing writing (cancellare la lavagna), deleting files and messages, and cancelling bookings or appointments. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Erase the board, please.

examples.it: Ho cancellato il messaggio per sbaglio.
examples.en: I deleted the message by mistake.
We will cancel the booking if it rains.

usage: Both saving a file on a computer or phone and saving someone's life; not used for saving money (that is 'risparmiare'). Regular -are verb.

examples.it: Salva il documento prima di chiudere il computer.
examples.en: Save the document before shutting down the computer.

examples.it: Il medico ha salvato la vita al bambino.
examples.en: The doctor saved the child's life.

examples.it: Se salverai le foto sul cloud, non le perderai.
examples.en: If you save the photos to the cloud, you won't lose them.

usage: Usually intransitive; with an object it means to breathe something in (respirare aria pulita). Regular -are verb. Also figurative: 'lasciami respirare' (give me a break).

examples.en: Breathe deeply.

examples.it: In montagna abbiamo respirato aria pulita.
examples.en: In the mountains we breathed clean air.

examples.it: Con il naso chiuso non respiro bene.
examples.en: With a blocked nose I can't breathe well.

en: to attend; to go to (a course, a place); to hang out with
usage: Takes a direct object with no preposition: 'frequentare un corso', 'frequentare l'università'. With people it means to see them regularly. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I attend an Italian course.
She went to university in Bologna.
Next year I will be in the third year.

en: to revise; to review; to pass by again
usage: In school contexts it means going over material again before a test. As an intransitive verb it means to come by again ('ripasso più tardi'). Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I revise the verbs every evening.
We went over all the grammar.

examples.it: Ripasserò la lezione prima del test.
examples.en: I will review the lesson before the test.

usage: Copying text, files and, at school, cheating by copying from a classmate ('copiare da qualcuno'). Regular -are verb: copio, copi, copia.

examples.en: Copy the sentence into your notebook.
He cheated by copying during the exam.
I will copy Anna's notes.

usage: Both the hobby (andare a pescare) and catching a fish; also 'pescare una carta' (to draw a card). Spelling change: an h is added before e/i (peschi, pescherò). Regular -are verb.

examples.en: My grandfather goes fishing every Sunday.
We caught three fish.

examples.it: Pescheremo nel lago vicino a casa.
examples.en: We will fish in the lake near home.

usage: Accepting invitations, offers, gifts and payment methods ('accettate carte di credito?'). With a verb it takes 'di' + infinitive. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I accept the invitation with pleasure.
They accepted our proposal.
Would you accept a job abroad?

usage: Very common in speech: 'Scherzo!' (just kidding), 'Scherzi?' (are you kidding?). 'Non scherzare' means to be serious. Regular -are verb, takes avere.

examples.en: I'm joking, it's not true!
We joked all evening.

examples.it: Scherzerà ancora, ma sotto sotto è preoccupato.
examples.en: He will keep joking, but deep down he is worried.

usage: The transitive counterpart of 'alzarsi': you lift or raise something (alzare la mano, il volume, la voce). Regular -are verb, takes avere.

examples.it: Alza la mano se hai una domanda.
examples.en: Raise your hand if you have a question.

examples.it: Ho alzato il volume della radio.
examples.en: I turned up the volume of the radio.

examples.it: Alzeremo il tavolo insieme, è pesante.
examples.en: We will lift the table together, it's heavy.

usage: Reflexive verb, takes essere. The imperative 'Rilassati!' is common. The non-reflexive 'rilassare' means to relax something (the muscles). Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I relax with music.
We relaxed at the seaside.
Relax, everything will be fine.

usage: A key classroom verb: 'Come si pronuncia?' (How do you pronounce it?). Regular -are verb; the i is dropped before e/i (pronunci, pronuncerò).

examples.en: How do you pronounce this word?

examples.it: Hai pronunciato benissimo il mio nome.
examples.en: You pronounced my name very well.

examples.it: Con la pratica pronuncerai meglio la 'r'.
examples.en: With practice you will pronounce the 'r' better.

en: to introduce oneself; to show up
usage: 'Mi presento' is the standard way to start introducing yourself. It also means to turn up somewhere (presentarsi al colloquio, presentarsi in ritardo). Reflexive, takes essere. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: Let me introduce myself: I'm Paolo.

examples.it: Si è presentata al colloquio in ritardo.
examples.en: She showed up late for the interview.
Report to the office at nine.

usage: Stronger and more enthusiastic than 'piacere': 'Adoro il gelato!'. Often used informally for things you really love; the religious meaning is to worship. Regular -are verb.

examples.en: I love pistachio ice cream.
She has always adored cats.
You will love this city, you'll see.

usage: Used for ice skating and roller skating ('pattinare sul ghiaccio', 'pattinare a rotelle'). Regular -are verb, takes avere.

examples.en: In winter we skate on the frozen lake.

examples.it: Ho pattinato per la prima volta a dieci anni.
examples.en: I skated for the first time when I was ten.
Would you go skating with me on Saturday?
